item.subject: science
item.chapter_label: Earth, Sun and the apparent motion of the sky
item.stem: Meena watches the night sky from her terrace in Jaipur. She notices that the Pole Star seems to stay in almost the same place all night, while the other stars seem to move around it. Why does the Pole Star appear nearly stationary?

options.A: Earth revolves around the Sun, so the stars make circular trails around the Pole Star
options.B: Earth's rotation axis points very close to the Pole Star, so it appears nearly fixed while other stars seem to move around it
options.C: The other stars orbit the Pole Star, so only they appear to move
options.D: The Pole Star is the nearly stationary centre of star trails in both the northern and southern hemispheres
